newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian minister urges higher food import duties.
newsitem.headline: Russian minister urges higher food import duties.

text.p: Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Zaveryukha said he has written to Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin calling for rises in import duties on a series of foods, especially flour, sugar and alcohol, Itar-Tass news agency said on Wednesday.
Tass quoted Zaveryukha, who is responsible for agriculture and the food industry, as saying that the agro-industrial sector would not emerge from crisis without extreme measures from the state.
Zaveryukha also told Russian television news that quotas on an unspecified series of food imports would be introduced from January 1997.
Other cabinet ministers have said Russia will not introduce protectionist curbs as they would be counter-productive and Russia cannot feed itself without imports.
But some officials have stepped up protectionist rhetoric in rcent months because of concern about domestic producers.
Imports account for up to 45 percent of the domestic food market, according to trade sources. --Jonathan Lynn, Moscow Newsroom, +7095 941 8520
